title: Investigation into woman's death is almost finished
article: Yukon RCMP have forwarded the results of their near-complete investigation into the in-custody death of a Tagish woman to the federal Crown's office, but it will be an Outside prosecutor who reviews the case.
"The investigation into the death in custody of Heather Benson is near completion, pending the technical reports," Sgt. Guy Rook, the M-Division spokesman, said in an interview Monday.
Benson died instantly when the police cruiser she was riding in, driven by a Carcross RCMP constable, crashed nearly two months ago.
"The investigation results, without the technical reports, have been forwarded to the Crown for review," said Rook. "Following their review, there will be our internal, independent review as well."
An RCMP officer from another division in Canada will conduct that independent review.
As well, the local Crown's office won't be handling the file, but is instead sending the investigation results to a prosecutor Outside.
"We felt that was the preferential way to deal with it," said Peter Chisholm, who heads up the Yukon's criminal prosecutors' office.
The local office received the RCMP's information package last week, and though Chisholm hasn't handed the Outside prosecutor a deadline, he expects an answer back in the next month.

When the RCMP forwards the findings of an investigation to the prosecutor's office, the police generally make recommendations about possible charges, though it's up to the Crown to decide what, if any, charges are laid against a person.
Rook wouldn't say if the RCMP have made any such recommendations in this case against the police officer who was driving the car in which Benson died.

But he stressed this is a special kind of case because the investigation focused on the actions of an RCMP officer, and regardless of whether charges against the constable are warranted, the Crown -- not the police -- will make the call.
"It becomes standard practice when it involves one of our own members," the sergeant said about forwarding the results of this sort of investigation to the Crown.
"We want to eliminate any perception of bias ... we recognize there's a higher scrutiny on the police and want to demonstrate that we realize that."
At about 5:45 a.m. on Sept. 27, Carcross RCMP's Const. Jeff Monkman was transporting Benson to Whitehorse for a court appearance. She'd been arrested on drug charges, but hadn't yet been charged.
Monkman crashed and rolled the police cruiser along the South Klondike Highway. He was uninjured, but the 37-year-old Benson died instantly.
Monkman was reassigned and is currently working as a uniformed general-duty constable on one of four Whitehorse detachment shifts.
Police have refused to say whether Benson was handcuffed or wearing a seatbelt at the time of the crash.
The details of Benson's death won't be made public until an as- yet unscheduled coroner's inquest. Such inquests are standard procedure when a person dies in police custody.
An M-Division collision reconstructionist and the force's major crimes unit investigated the matter along with the coroner.
